text: Flag transactions that are far above the customer's typical transaction amount, especially when the merchant is unfamiliar.
Treat rapid transactions in different cities or countries as high risk because they may indicate card testing or account takeover.
Review unusual time-of-day activity when a customer suddenly transacts during hours that differ from their normal pattern.
Escalate first-time high-value transactions to a new merchant when there is no prior customer relationship with that merchant.
Flag sudden spikes in transaction frequency, especially many small purchases within a short time window.
Review repeated declined attempts followed by an approved purchase because this can indicate credential stuffing or limit probing.
Treat purchases from high-risk merchant categories as suspicious when they differ from the customer's historical spending behavior.
Flag transactions where the billing location, shipping location, and device location are inconsistent with the customer's profile.
Review new-device transactions when the device has no trusted history and the transaction amount is unusually large.
Escalate transactions that combine multiple weak fraud signals, such as a new merchant, unusual hour, high amount, and unfamiliar location.
